title: Atomic Theory and Structure - Chemistry - Bohr Model
subject: Chemistry

questions.q: In the Bohr model of the hydrogen atom, electrons are described as:
options: Moving freely in a random cloud
Orbiting the nucleus in fixed, quantized energy levels
Stationary at fixed distances from the nucleus
questions.explain: Bohr proposed that electrons move in specific circular orbits (energy levels) around the nucleus and cannot exist between these levels.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What occurs when an electron in an atom moves from a higher energy level ($n=3$) to a lower energy level ($n=2$)?
options: Energy is absorbed in the form of a photon.
Energy is emitted in the form of a photon.
The atom becomes a negative ion.
questions.explain: When an electron falls to a lower energy state, the difference in energy is released (emitted) as electromagnetic radiation (light).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: The lowest possible energy state of an atom is called the:
questions.explain: The ground state is the lowest energy level an electron can occupy. Any higher level is an excited state.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which transition in a hydrogen atom would result in the emission of the photon with the **highest** energy?
questions.explain: Energy gaps between levels decrease as $(n)$ increases. The gap between $n=1$ and $n=2$ is the largest energy difference, resulting in the highest energy photon.
